conventions.convention: The unconstrained force branch uses N ≥ 1 labels, fixed positive inertial masses, a nondegenerate open time window I₀, an open configuration domain Q ⊆ R^(3N), and unrestricted coordinate velocities. Forces are continuous and locally Lipschitz in the complete state (x,v), locally uniformly in time.

The associated first-order field is (v,M⁻¹F), with M⁻¹ dividing each label's force by its own inertial mass. Motions are C² position curves; included interval endpoints use domain-relative one-sided derivatives.

Frame changes have t′=t+b and xᵢ′=Rxᵢ+υt+a₀, with R ∈ SO(3). Forces transfer by rotation and inverse affine substitution on the transferred open domain; a proper configuration domain can become time-dependent.

Antisymmetry, centrality and potential presentation are additional declared restrictions. Potential forces have Fᵢ=−∇ₓᵢU with U ∈ C². Gravitational couplings are distinct from inertial masses unless their identification is separately adopted.

The breakdown conclusion quantifies an outside point in every terminal interval for each compact set. State-space escape is asserted when I₀=R; autonomous compact trapping is applied to the extended-time model on R.

Linear drag is −cv in a declared medium-rest frame, with c ≥ 0 of dimension mass/time. The terminal-velocity formula requires c > 0. The oscillator-specific fluctuation criterion is not imposed on the free-particle drag model.
Projectile data require g > 0, v₀ > 0 and 0 < α < π/2; flight time means the positive return to launch height, and range is the horizontal displacement at that return.

The continuity-only counterexample explicitly drops the Lipschitz clause, uses unit inertial mass, and declares a force scale λ and reference length ℓ*. It is outside the adopted regular force branch.

All parameters and worked numerical data are declared model inputs, not observations. Measured replacements would carry their empirical conditions and uncertainty; the computations establish conditional model consequences.

load_bearing.statement: Adopts continuous, state-locally-Lipschitz force maps on I₀ × Q × R^(3N), the equation mᵢxᵢ″=Fᵢ(t,x,x′), pointwise additive composition, and the specified Galilean transfer law.
Defines the associated system z′=(v,M⁻¹F), C² motions and their equivalence with first-order solutions, initial data, unique maximal motions, and Φ(t;t₀,z₀) on the actual maximal intervals.

Every admissible datum has a local motion, any two motions with the same datum agree on their common interval, and there is exactly one maximal motion on an open interval. On the stated cylinder, hM ≤ r and Λh < 1 give exactly one motion whose state graph lies in that cylinder.

Separately adopts external-plus-pair presentations, optional antisymmetry and centrality, C² potential presentations with Fᵢ=−∇ₓᵢU, and the collision-excluded Newtonian gravitational pair potential with distinct gravitational coupling parameters.

At a finite maximal right endpoint, every compact K ⊆ D and every terminal interval contain a graph point outside K. Terminal compact trapping would give an extension. On I₀=R, either the state is unbounded on every terminal interval or positions approach Qᶜ in the explicitly quantified sense.
Adopts F(t,x,v)=m g−cv on R × R³ × R³, with m > 0, c ≥ 0, declared constant g, medium-rest-frame interpretation, and phenomenological regime and fluctuation qualifications.
For Fᵢ=mᵢg on the full configuration space and time window R, xᵢ(t)=x₀,ᵢ+v₀,ᵢt+g t²/2 is the unique maximal motion; the model transfers to a uniform-force model with g′=Rg.

concerns.concern: Definition (c) writes “the state curve z=(x,x′):J→D” and repeatedly says z(t) ∈ D, although D=I₀×Q×R^(3N) includes time and has dimension 1+6N. The pair z takes values in Q×R^(3N); its graph (t,z(t)) takes values in D. The intended equivalence is clear, but the displayed map and memberships are mistyped.

The final frame-covariance remark says “a motion's maximal interval is unchanged by a time shift between frames.” Under the declared convention t′=t+b, the coordinate interval is Jmax+b, rather than literally Jmax. The interval's duration and maximality are preserved.

Clause (vi) says “When Q=R^(3N) — the case of the models of the companion page —”. The companion page also contains the inverse-square external model with Q=R³\{0}, both in ex-cm02-force-model-regularity-checks and cex-cm02-singular-collision-finite-time. The parenthetical inaccurately describes the companion inventory; the surrounding transferred-domain rule itself accommodates proper Q.

Clause (iii) proves the state-Lipschitz inequality only for states “sharing a position”, then concludes a global state-Lipschitz constant. The missing unrestricted comparison is immediate because F does not depend on position: for z=(x,v), z′=(x′,v′), the same force difference is c|v−v′| ≤ c|z−z′|. The companion regularity example supplies that complete comparison.

alerts.finding: In clause (i), post-cm15-impulse requires “a motion x=(x₁,x₂):I→Q of the associated first-order system ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]])” before imposing its piecewise-C² and finite-jump clauses. The cited definition requires a C² motion on its entire interval, equivalently a differentiable state solution; consequently its velocities are continuous and J=0. That prerequisite excludes the intended nonzero impulses and conflicts with the postulate's stated extension status. The candidate needs its own piecewise motion notion, with the smooth-system requirement confined to times away from t*. Also, the quoted first-order solution has state (x,x′), not position x alone.

The smooth-force exclusion in pthm-cm15-impact-balance is faithful, but post-cm15-impulse clause (i) calls its finite-jump candidate a motion of the cited smooth first-order system. This excludes nonzero jumps; see the routed alert.

The stability definition distinguishes maximality on a declared open restriction from maximality for the supplier's full product domain. Smooth flow and variational properties require additional hypotheses/suppliers.
Admissible smooth linear forces and explicitly verified all-time curves are identified with maximal motions using uniqueness; chaos is not inferred merely from deterministic evolution.
Observation times must lie inside the unique maximal motion's interval. Measurement, calibration and sampling assumptions remain separate from deterministic prediction.

Zero-force prediction curves are verified directly. Frame-transfer protocol interpretation explicitly requires an admissible fixed-domain presentation; statistical outcomes are not deduced from Newtonian uniqueness.
